data.headline: SPY: separate long-rate relief from a flatter curve.
data.summary: Broad US equity valuations and company financing can respond differently to the Treasury curve. November 2 brought a lower ten-year yield but a higher two-year yield, narrowing their spread. That mixed rates backdrop adds context to SPY without establishing its opening level or sector returns.

bull.text: The ten-year Treasury yield was 4.91% on November 2, down 3 basis points from October 30. A lower long-rate benchmark can support a valuation interpretation, conditional on earnings and risk premiums that are not measured here.

bear.text: The two-year yield increased 3 basis points to 4.59%. The ten-year-minus-two-year spread narrowed from 38 to 32 basis points; curve flattening is a distinct observation, not proof of weaker growth or a uniform benefit to SPY constituents.

watch.text: S&P futures asset managers held net long 923,449 contracts and leveraged funds net short 400,604 on October 27. Keep those lagged positions separate from SPY share flows and the newly collected rates observations.
The decline in reverse-repo usage to $0.427 billion on November 3 is a money-market facility reading. It does not reveal how much capital, if any, moved into broad equities.

limitations: Treasury yields describe November 2; SOFR and reverse-repo figures describe November 3. These are delayed official observations, not live prices or the market response to a release.
CFTC figures are October 27 futures-only category positions. Related futures differ from ETF shares and do not identify current purchases, fund flows or individual investors.
Current ETF prices, option chains, gamma, representative social sentiment and dark-pool direction remain independently unmeasured. Hosted displays are separate from saved evidence.
The interpretation describes possible transmission channels, not measured causation, a return prediction or a calibrated trading probability. No prospective model is qualified.
